subject: POC infrastructure decision & ownership worksheet
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Olsen <dana.olson@lynxhealth.com>, Matt Li <matt.li@lynxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + POC infra options (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Hi Dana + Matt —

Thanks again for a productive demo this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture next steps and surface the three POC environment options so Lynx can pick the path that minimizes lift while meeting your security and evaluation goals. Summary below + an attached one-page working MOP (mutual action plan) you can edit.

Quick recap of evaluation goals (as we heard them):
- Accuracy: summary and classification precision on sample discharge notes (target: >88% F1 on our baseline prompts)
- Latency: median token latency under 80ms for 256-token completions in the primary region (US-West)
- Data controls: customer owns logs, no persistent model training on PII, audit trail for inference requests
- Cost cap: pilot run budget ~ $6k/month for 250k tokens/day peak during evaluation window

POC environment options (high level):
1) Hosted API (fastest)
   - Pros: zero infra setup, immediate onboarding, Redwood-managed runtime, streaming responses, built-in telemetry
   - Cons: data lives in Redwood-hosted environment (we can sign a scoped DPA and SOC2 controls, but not VPC-level network isolation)
   - Timeline estimate: 2 business days to spin up the trial account and seed prompts

2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity)
   - Pros: isolated GPU pool, predictable throughput, custom autoscale and batch settings; logs exported to your SIEM via secure endpoint
   - Cons: requires commitment for reserved capacity for the POC window (monthly), slightly longer setup (3–5 business days)

3) VPC Private deployment (customer-managed network)
   - Pros: full network isolation, KMS integration, ideal for PHI workflows when required by policy
   - Cons: most effort (network configs, firewall, peering), estimated 2–3 weeks (depending on network approvals)

Recommendation (based on your goals): start with Hosted API to prove quality and latency quickly, then run a short dedicated sandbox if you want to validate sustained throughput and cost at scale. If Policy requires it, we can move to VPC for the production handoff.

Next actions / owners (proposal):
- Lynx: confirm which environment option you want to start with and identify network owner (Dana / IT) — due Fri 3/3
- Redwood (Vivek): deliver a seeded test project with sample prompts, success criterion dashboard, and billing estimate — by Mon 3/6
- Redwood (Ben): provide dedicated sandbox pricing and capacity options if chosen — by Tue 3/7
- Lynx: share sample data subset and approve DPA scoping (if Hosted) or network checklist (if VPC) — by Mon 3/6

I've attached a one-page editable MOP (redwood-poc-mop.xlsx) and our network checklist template (lynx-network-checklist.pdf).

If you're comfortable, reply with the option you want to start with and we'll lock dates.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- redwood-poc-mop.xlsx (spreadsheet, edit in Drive)
- lynx-network-checklist.pdf (PDF, network/VPC checklist)

From: Dana Olsen <dana.olson@lynxhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt Li <matt.li@lynxhealth.com>, procurement@lynxhealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + POC infra options (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Vivek — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) The compliance bar: some of the notes contain limited PHI. Our security team prefers VPC for any POC with PHI, but they may accept a scoped Hosted instance if we can ensure no training/retention and receive an auditable request log.
2) Timeline sensitivity: we want results for the internal clinical review on 3/20. Starting Hosted today would make that easy. VPC is likely too slow for the 3/20 deadline unless we parallel-path.

Given that, we're leaning toward starting Hosted for functional evaluation and simultaneously opening a ticket to scope VPC if it looks promising. Can you confirm whether the Hosted option gives us:  
- a) request-level audit logs exportable to our S3 (read-only)
- b) a contractual clause prohibiting model training on our inputs during the POC

Also, can Ben provide a high-level estimate for the Dedicated sandbox cost so procurement can see options?

Thanks — Dana
Director, Product Operations
Lynx Health

On Wed, Mar 1, 2028 at 3:12 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap + POC infra options (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Vivek / Monica —

Quick internal note before we reply to Lynx: for Dedicated sandbox pricing, here's a rough tiered estimate we can share as a ballpark for procurement:
- Small (2x A10G-equivalent, 500k tokens/day): $7,500 / month (reserved during trial)
- Medium (4x A10G-equivalent, 1.2M tokens/day): $13,500 / month
- Large (8x, heavy throughput): $24,000 / month

We should make it clear these include reserved capacity and support hours for scaling. If they start Hosted and escalate, we can credit them for the first month toward Dedicated reservation costs (partial credit) — helps procurement sign off.

Also note: Hosted can export request logs to an S3 bucket via a signed transfer (we'll still retain our own operational logs for 30 days unless otherwise contracted). We can add the contractual language forbidding training on customer inputs in the DPA/contract addendum.

I'll prepare a short pricing appendix and a suggested credit clause. Monica — can you review the credit wording and margin impact?

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Final: POC option selection & mutual action plan (next steps)

Thanks Dana — this aligns with our plan. Per your ask, here's the consolidated next steps and timeline. Please reply with a short confirmation ("Start Hosted") so we can provision immediately.

Mutual Action Plan (finalized):
- Lynx: Confirm "Start Hosted" or "Start Dedicated" by EOD 3/7 (owner: Dana)
- Lynx: Deliver sample dataset (anonymized subset) and S3 path for log export (if Hosted) — due 3/9 (owner: Matt)
- Redwood (Vivek): Provision Hosted trial workspace, seed prompts, and run initial 10k-token perf pass — by 3/10
- Redwood (Ben): Send Dedicated sandbox appendix if Lynx chooses Dedicated; include credit proposal — by 3/9
- Security/legal: Draft a scoped addendum to the DPA (no model training on POC inputs; 30-day retention on infer logs unless otherwise agreed) — Redwood legal to share by 3/11

Success criteria (to validate during the POC):
- >= 88% F1 on the annotated discharge note set (we'll provide script)
- Median token latency <80ms for 256-token completions in US-West
- Audit log export to your S3 and confirmation of receipt

Attachments included for reference: redwood-poc-mop.xlsx (editable MOP), lynx-network-checklist.pdf (if you later need VPC)

If you want to parallel-path VPC scoping, we can open the network onboarding ticket now — I recommend Hosted first given your 3/20 review date.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
